title: Browser QA evidence, repair loop, and Generation Report model
question: Which Browser QA model gives Meridian reproducible viewport and state evidence, behavioral accessibility checks, stale screenshot rejection, bounded repair, and a Human review boundary without treating automated checks as conformance?

scope.summary: Compare a digest-bound behavioral matrix with screenshot-golden-only testing, then exercise the selected contract against synthetic Team Invitation and Issue Triage fixtures.

constraints: Automated evidence cannot claim WCAG conformance or replace manual assistive-technology evaluation.
Every screenshot is bound to the exact Manifest, Review UI, Review Model, Usage Manifest, Policy, browser, and platform.
Desktop, 768px Tablet, and 375px Mobile are required for every applicable Screen and State.
Critical or Major findings block final Human review; Direction pairwise comparison remains the earlier M3 gate.
Visual repair cannot modify locked requirements, responsibilities, selected patterns, selected direction, capability plan, or adapter selection.
At most two repair rounds are permitted.

criteria.name: Evidence integrity
criteria.description: Rejects stale, partial, duplicate, or environment-ambiguous capture evidence.

criteria.name: Behavioral coverage
criteria.description: Covers viewport reflow, state signals, keyboard reachability, focus visibility, semantics, and runtime provenance.

criteria.name: Repair governance
criteria.description: Routes findings to the owning layer, preserves locked structure, enforces a repair limit, and stops before Human review when blockers remain.

candidates.name: Digest-bound behavioral Browser QA matrix
candidates.license: Meridian owns the evidence contract; Playwright remains under its published project license.

assessments.notes: Source and screenshot digests plus an exact derived matrix are implemented; real capture validation is pending execution.
The contract combines screenshots with keyboard, focus, semantics, state, overflow, console, and provenance checks.
Layer classification, locked-structure digest, bounded repair, Human escalation, and evidence-gated Generation Report are implemented; real Browser evidence remains pending.

limitations: Chromium evidence does not cover every browser engine or platform accessibility API.
Pixel output varies by platform and must retain environment provenance.

candidates.name: Screenshot golden comparison only
candidates.license: Uses Playwright visual comparison APIs under the project license; Meridian owns baselines and review policy.

assessments.notes: Golden files are reviewable and environment-specific, but do not by themselves prove the complete Manifest-derived matrix.
Pixel comparison cannot prove keyboard reachability, accessible names, ARIA references, state announcements, or runtime provenance.
A changed golden records appearance drift but does not identify the owning design layer or protect locked structure.

limitations: Rendering differs across OS, browser, settings, and hardware.
A visually matching screenshot can retain semantic and keyboard failures.

evidence.title: Playwright Emulation
evidence.summary: Playwright supports explicit browser contexts and viewport, touch, locale, color scheme, and device emulation; viewport size can be fixed per context or page.
limitations: Device emulation does not reproduce every physical device or assistive-technology behavior.

evidence.title: Playwright Screenshots
evidence.summary: Playwright can capture full-page, element, file, or buffer screenshots, allowing Meridian to hash the exact PNG bytes.
limitations: The screenshot API does not define Meridian's completeness or stale-source rules.

evidence.title: Playwright Visual Comparisons
evidence.summary: Playwright stores platform-qualified reference screenshots and warns that rendering varies with OS, version, settings, hardware, power, and headless mode.
limitations: Pixel comparison alone cannot establish semantic or behavioral correctness.

evidence.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2
evidence.summary: WCAG 2.2 defines Reflow, Keyboard, Focus Order, Focus Visible, Focus Not Obscured, and Name, Role, Value requirements relevant to the matrix.
limitations: Passing selected automated checks does not establish conformance with all success criteria.

evidence.title: Developing a Keyboard Interface
evidence.summary: APG describes the tab sequence, composite focus management, and the requirement that the visual focus indicator remain visible.
limitations: APG is guidance and not a replacement for normative WCAG evaluation.

evidence.title: Accessibility Conformance Testing Overview
evidence.summary: ACT formalizes transparent automated, semi-automated, and manual test rules while keeping individual rules informative rather than equating them with complete conformance.
limitations: Meridian's local checks are ACT-informed but are not claimed as formally approved ACT Rules.

spikes.title: Two-pilot Generic Review UI Browser QA spike
spikes.hypothesis: A Manifest-derived matrix with behavioral checks and digest-bound screenshots will detect failures that screenshot-only review cannot classify or safely repair.
findings: QA Policy, Evidence schema, deterministic finding classification, and two synthetic Pilot chains are implemented.
Issue Triage now contains long Japanese content and ten rows to satisfy explicit stress thresholds.
The capture runner is pinned to Playwright 1.62.0 and derives every expected scenario from Manifest screenRefs and state fixtures.
Repair limits, AI locked-layer prohibition, Human escalation, and Generation Report approval digest are implemented and covered by deterministic tests.
Fixture Generation Reports are generated as evidence-missing and cannot advance to Human approval without real Browser QA evidence.
Real headless Chromium capture is pending because the current execution permission quota rejected browser launch; no screenshot or pass claim has been recorded.

unresolvedItems: Run the complete two-Pilot Chromium capture matrix and validate screenshot digests.
Compare observed evidence coverage before recommending a candidate.
Human approval remains required after the decision becomes decision-ready.
revisitTriggers: A required browser engine cannot reproduce the evidence
Manual assistive-technology testing contradicts automated findings
Repair classification repeatedly points to locked structure
